text:
elaine: Heads-up — observed a big spike in eviction fanout during yesterday's canary. A bunch of duplicate eviction requests hit the control plane and generated noisy telemetry. Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private seem to diverge here. Can we discuss mode-specific heuristics?

sam: Do you have the alert/graph links? curious about rate and cardinality.

elaine: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/evictions?panel=12 — check the bushy tail at ~14:03. ops-bot posted the alert too: `EVCTION_FANOUT_HIGH` (stacked retries).

marta: I pulled traces — looks like when a transient node loss happened, the coordinator fanout loop didn't short-circuit for private deployments because the sidecar probe timeouts are longer. Hosted had aggressive TTL so less duplication.

pranav: That matches my read. Two orthogonal issues: (1) control-plane fanout logic is one-size-fits-all, (2) telemetry tags don't include hosting_mode in some of the eviction spans, so it's hard to filter.

elaine: Proposal sketch: add a small policy surface so fanout behavior can be tuned by hosting_mode. e.g.:

```
eviction_policy:
  hosted:
    max_fanout: 12
    short_circuit_delay_ms: 25
  dedicated:
    max_fanout: 8
    short_circuit_delay_ms: 50
  private:
    max_fanout: 6
    short_circuit_delay_ms: 120
```

Keep defaults conservative. Thoughts?

sam: I like per-mode knobs. Two cautions: (a) lowering fanout reduces repair speed when a large pool actually fails, so we need to ensure fallback (e.g., staggered rounds) doesn't increase window of degraded capacity, (b) don't add knobs without telemetry to validate.

marta: +1 — we should also add `hosting_mode` to eviction traces and a `fanout_reason` tag. That way we can split SLOs and set alerts per-mode.

pranav: Another idea: probabilistic short-circuiting. On first failure, instead of immediately broadcasting to N peers, do a quick precheck (single probe) and, if still needed, expand with exponential fanout. That bounds worst-case duplicates.

derek: Implementation tradeoffs: precheck adds latency on the happy path. We could gate the slower precheck behind a feature flag for canary regions. Also consider a small per-tenant circuit-breaker token so rapid repeated evictions get suppressed for Xs.

elaine: Sounds good. For rollout: 1) Add tracing tags + telemetry dashboards; 2) Add hosting_mode policy fields with sane defaults; 3) Implement probabilistic/exponential fanout behind FF; 4) Enable in one region for 24h with heavy load tests.

marta: Q: how do we compute `max_fanout` safely? Should it be absolute or relative to pool size? Absolute feels simpler but could be wrong for tiny pools.

pranav: Make it `min(max_fanout, pool_size-1)` in code. And add a `fanout_scale: relative|absolute` flag if teams want custom behavior. Keep default relative for safety.

sam: Also add a metric `eviction.vectors_suppressed` for when circuit-breaker stops a fanout; it helps validate correctness.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Note: there's a previously scheduled job touching eviction logic next week (PR #4721). Recommend coordinating sequence to avoid merge conflicts.

derek: I'll own the RFC + implementation plan. I'll propose a minimal API for `eviction_policy` and a rollout checklist. Can we aim for a spec PR by EOD Friday?

elaine: Thanks — please include a small synthetic test harness that can emulate node flaps and measure duplicate request counts. We should show numeric improvements before cutting defaults.

pranav: I'll prep the telemetry dashboard templates and add `hosting_mode` to the trace pipeline.

marta: If we do probabilistic short-circuiting, include a deterministic seed option for tests so results are reproducible.

sam: Reminder: consider cost/latency SLO matrix – less fanout reduces egress + CPU, but may increase tail latency for recoveries. Add a short section to the RFC quantifying this with a couple of worst-case scenarios.

elaine: Great. If no objections, this thread is the decision to proceed with the RFC + small telemetry first. Derek — ping me when PR is ready and I'll review. :thumbsup:
